title: How Long Would You Last on the Moon Without a Spacesuit? #shorts
description_hook: You step onto the Moon in full Sun with no spacesuit. No air, wild temperatures, and the clock starts now.

beats.say: How long would you last on the Moon without a spacesuit? You step out into full Sun. The ground is about 127 degrees Celsius.
beats.img: a lone human silhouette in plain clothes standing on bright grey lunar dust under a harsh white sun, pitch black sky above, long sharp shadow

beats.say: You weigh one-sixth of what you do on Earth. Every step turns into a slow, floating bounce.
beats.img: a small figure seen from behind mid-leap above a cratered lunar plain, a puff of fine dust hanging below its feet, black starless sky

beats.say: Now take a breath. There is no air here, only a thin exosphere. Nothing fills your lungs.
beats.img: an empty silent lunar horizon with the blue Earth hanging low in a black sky, no haze at all, razor sharp crater edges

beats.say: And cosmic rays keep falling: about 1369 microsieverts a day, 2.6 times the dose inside the space station. Slow, but relentless.
beats.img: faint streaks of cosmic rays raining down through the darkness onto a barren grey crater floor, glowing particle trails, cold eerie light

gumi.say: Gumi's odds: zero. Step into shadow and it plummets to about minus 173 degrees Celsius.
